title: Steer the Ship
speaker: Eko Jeff Kelley
summary: Eko Jeff Kelley invites listeners to explore their mental habits and patterns that perpetuate suffering by cultivating awareness and intention to interrupt them, viewing these patterns as workable and observable like other habits. By doing so, they aim to develop a more spacious relationship with their mind and reality, embodying the principles of Bodhisattva practice through subtle efforts to transform patterns such as anger or fear without judgment. This approach involves stepping forward into new life with compassion and gentleness, finding support in one's true nature and experiencing freedom and open-heartedness in the present moment.
topics: "stepping off the top of a hundred foot pole"

They are observable, and once we observe them like other habits, we can choose to do things differently.
We can take a different route, and they are like some habits, they are deeply ingrained, many of them, and so they take a lot of time to unravel or to step out of.
And because our life, our world is greatly conditioned by our mind, our reality is greatly determined by the mental lens through which we view it, which consists of habits.
